metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Missouri (2026):Rules, Exemptions & Examples

description: Missouri base sales tax is 4.225%. Qualifying precious-metal bullion is fully exempt; jewelry and nonqualifying collectibles are taxable. Check local rules.

What's covered by the exemption
Qualifying precious-metal bullion
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Even when the state-level rule is clear, cities or counties in this state may charge their own tax. Here's what to expect.
Local treatment
Check local conformity
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Missouri.
Is gold and silver bullion taxable in Missouri?
+
No. Missouri fully exempts qualifying precious-metal bullion from sales tax.
Do purity or form rules matter for the Missouri bullion exemption?
+
Yes. Missouri’s exemption applies only to bullion that meets the state’s purity/form requirements for qualifying bullion.
Are numismatic or collectible coins taxed in Missouri?
+
It depends. Coins are conditional—items that qualify as bullion can be exempt, while nonqualifying collectibles may be taxable.
Is precious-metal jewelry taxed in Missouri?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable even though qualifying bullion is exempt.
Do local Missouri taxes follow the same bullion exemption?
+
Not always. Check local conformity because local tax treatment may differ even when the state exemption applies.
